fix_subject: Fixing the arguments used in auxiliary hypre function call
defect: New ParAdd calls internal::hypre_ParCSRMatrixAdd(*A,*B,&C) with three arguments, but the function takes two and returns the matrix, so it does not compile.
The new ParAdd calls internal::hypre_ParCSRMatrixAdd(*A, *B, &C) with three arguments, but the helper takes two and returns the matrix, so it does not compile.

fix_subject: Fixed a seg fault when you try to use a CurlCurl integrator without supplying a coeff.
defect: After the restructuring, the else branch calls MQ->Eval whenever Q is null, which dereferences a null pointer when neither Q nor MQ is supplied.
CurlCurlIntegrator::AssembleElementMatrix now takes the MQ branch whenever Q is null, dereferencing a null MQ (segfault) when the integrator has no coefficient at all.
createMeshBlueprintAdjacencies creates adjacency groups and zero-length views for every group, including groups with no vertices or neighbors, which Sidre/Conduit reject with invalid-cast warnings.

createMeshBlueprintAdjacencies creates an adjacency group with zero-length views for every processor group, including groups that share no vertices, which yields invalid empty blueprint entries and Sidre/Conduit invalid-cast warnings.

fix_subject: Fixing bug when getting Hypre version.
defect: The new file assigns HYPRE_RELEASE_VERSION/HYPRE_PACKAGE_VERSION directly to a const char*, but HYPRE_config.h defines the version unquoted, so it must be stringized.
The new tool uses HYPRE_RELEASE_VERSION/HYPRE_PACKAGE_VERSION directly as a string literal, but hypre's config header can define it unquoted, so the version detection does not compile or parse.
The new GetBareDofs maps edges always to ghost-dof offsets (ndofs+ngvdofs+index*ne) regardless of whether the edge is regular or ghost, and GetBareFaceDofs is an empty TODO.
The new GetBareDofs treats every entity as a ghost: vertices go through GetGhostVertexDofs and edges get ndofs + ngvdofs + index*ne, so regular (non-ghost) vertices and edges get wrong DOF numbers.

fix_subject: Fixed a problem with col_map_offd in MakeHypreMatrix.
defect: MakeHypreMatrix numbers off-diagonal columns in order of first appearance, so col_map_offd is not sorted ascending as hypre requires.
MakeHypreMatrix numbers the off-diagonal columns in order of first appearance, so col_map_offd (cmap) is not sorted ascending as hypre requires, and the HypreParMatrix is invalid.

BuildVertexList indexes vertex_list.conforming by nd.vert_index without checking for -1 and sizes it by vertex_nodeId.Size(), so nodes without a vertex index cause out-of-bounds access and ghost vertices are mishandled.

The new BuildVertexList indexes vertex_list.conforming[nd.vert_index] without checking vert_index >= 0, calls ElementSharesVertex for such nodes, and resizes conforming up front, which leaves default entries for unvisited slots.
ComplexSparseMatrix::GetSystemMatrix offsets the imaginary/real block column indices by nrows instead of the number of columns, wrong for rectangular matrices.

ComplexSparseMatrix::GetSystemMatrix shifts the column indices of the second block column by nrows instead of the number of columns, giving wrong (or out-of-range) column indices for rectangular blocks.

In the new scaled Norml2, when a larger entry is found the code sets sum = 1 + (scale/absdata)^2 instead of 1 + sum*(scale/absdata)^2, which drops the earlier accumulated terms and gives a wrong norm.
When a larger entry is found, the new scaled Norml2 resets sum = 1 + (scale/absdata)^2 instead of rescaling the old sum, so it returns wrong norms.

fix_subject: Fixed up the sundials 3 integration and predicated the sundials and petsc tests on those libraries being active
defect: The pure virtual SolveSystem changed its weight parameter from const Vector& to Vector&, so existing overrides (examples/sundials ex10, ex16, ...) no longer override it and the classes become abstract/fail to compile.

Changing the pure virtual SolveSystem parameter from 'const Vector &' to 'Vector &' means the derived classes in the SUNDIALS examples, still declared with const Vector &, no longer override it and stay abstract, so they fail to compile.

fix_subject: Fixing typos and adding a missing declaration
defect: The new PRISM case uses an undeclared identifier Time (typo for Times) and an undeclared variable m, so it does not compile.
The new PRISM case uses the misspelled identifier 'Time' instead of 'Times' and the variable m, which is only declared locally inside the TETRAHEDRON case, so geom.cpp does not compile.

When moving GetFaceBaseGeometry inline, the fallback returns BaseGeom (element geometry) instead of BaseFaceGeom, a cut-and-paste error giving the wrong face geometry for out-of-range or default calls.

When GetFaceBaseGeometry was moved inline into the header, its fallback was copied as BaseGeom (the element geometry) instead of BaseFaceGeom, so with no faces or i out of range it returns the element geometry.

fix_subject: Fixing a vertex numbering issue related to the lack of new vertices on triangular faces of uniformly refined prisms
defect: ParMesh::PriUniformRefinement computes the shared quad-face center vertex as oface + face index, while Mesh::PriUniformRefinement numbers those vertices oface + quad-face index (triangle faces get no new vertex).

The new ParMesh::PriUniformRefinement numbers the centre vertex of a shared quadrilateral face as oface + (global face index), but serial Mesh::PriUniformRefinement adds centre vertices only for quad faces (triangular faces get none), so the vertex numbers are wrong.

fix_subject: In class ParBlockNonlinearForm, add BlockVector members that serve as wrappers for true-dof block-vectors. This change also fixes a bug in the method GetLocalGradient(): 'block_offsets' was used instead of 'block_trueOffsets'.
defect: ParBlockNonlinearForm::GetGradient now delegates to GetLocalGradient, which offsets the true-dof input with block_offsets instead of block_trueOffsets, so the parallel gradient is evaluated at the wrong state.

ParBlockNonlinearForm::GetGradient now delegates to GetLocalGradient(x), which offsets the true-dof vector with block_offsets instead of block_trueOffsets, so the parallel gradient is assembled from wrongly sliced input.
The new miniapp does not compile: the typo ector, a trailing comma in a parameter list, undefined speed, mesh and dudt, a wrong ODE constructor call, and the wrong Step signature.

The new miniapp does not compile: ector typo, a trailing comma in a parameter list, the undeclared speed and mesh, dudt used under the name du_dt, an ODE(a) call against a two-argument constructor, and a Step with the wrong arity.

fix_subject: Bugfix in nd triangular face dof remapping
defect: The new k1 and k2 formulas use 2*pm1 instead of 2*pm2, giving out-of-range or wrong face DOF permutations (for p=2, k1=2 with only 2 DOFs).
The new k1/k2 formulas for the triangle face DoF orientations (1,0,2) and (2,0,1) use 2*pm1 where 2*pm2 is needed, giving wrong or out-of-range indices (for p=2 they yield 2,3 on a 2-DoF face).

fix_subject: Bugfix related to precedence of '?' operator
defect: In H1_PyramidElement::CalcDShape, expressions like '-1.0 + (z<1.0) ? a : 0.0' parse as '(-1.0 + (z<1.0)) ? a : 0.0' because of '?:' precedence, giving wrong derivatives (and dshape(1,0) also has the wrong sign).

In the new H1_PyramidElement::CalcDShape, expressions like -1.0 + (z<1.0) ? a : 0.0 parse as (-1.0 + (z<1.0)) ? a : 0.0 because '+' binds tighter than '?:', and dshape(1,0) also has the wrong sign/offset, so the derivatives are wrong.

fix_subject: Fixed some issues that came up during testing.
defect: Set{Par,Serial}DiscreteTargetSpec only set the evaluator's meta info and initial field when adapt_eval is NULL, so a user-supplied evaluator or a second call never gets the (new) target field, which ComputeAtNewPosition now relies on.

Set{Par,Serial}DiscreteTargetSpec now set meta info and the initial field only when adapt_eval is NULL, so a user-supplied evaluator (SetAdaptivityEvaluator) or a repeated call never gets its mesh/initial field set; the old code refreshed ts_nodes on every call.

fix_subject: fix error checks, clean up ex9, running with new interface
defect: The new option-setting code checks MFEM_ASSERT(retval != CV_SUCCESS/ARK_SUCCESS, ...), an inverted check that aborts on success in debug builds.
The added MFEM_ASSERT(retval != CV_SUCCESS / ARK_SUCCESS, ...) checks are inverted, so debug builds abort whenever the SUNDIALS calls succeed.

fix_subject: fix error checks, clean up ex9, running with new interface
defect: The new PrintInfo methods (and the modified ARKStepSetMassFn check) assert 'flag < 0' or 'flag != CV_SUCCESS', inverted checks that fire on success.
The new PrintInfo methods (and the SetMassFn check) use inverted asserts such as MFEM_ASSERT(flag < 0, ...), which fail in debug builds whenever the call succeeds.
The new ReadI/WriteI/... accessors pass Height() as the size of I, but the CSR row pointer has Height()+1 entries.

The new ReadI/WriteI/ReadWriteI accessors (and their Host variants) use Height() as the size of the CSR row-pointer array I, which actually has Height()+1 entries, so the last entry is never transferred.

fix_subject: Fixed a bug in ParallelDerefinementMatrix (crash due to bad diag matrix).
defect: ParallelDerefinementMatrix switches the diag SparseMatrix to the fixed-row-size constructor (ldof entries per row) for single-geometry meshes, which crashes as rows are not filled as that format requires.
ParallelDerefinementMatrix now builds the diag SparseMatrix with the fixed-row-size constructor (row size ldof) for single-geometry meshes, which produces a bad matrix and crashes.

fix_subject: fix to set maa before KINInit()
defect: KINSolver::SetMAA calls KINSetMAA directly on sundials_mem, but the acceleration space size must be set before KINInit (and sundials_mem may not exist yet), so the setting is ineffective or fails.
The new SetMAA calls KINSetMAA on sundials_mem after KINInit (done in SetOperator), when KINSOL requires maa before KINInit, and on a null sundials_mem if called before SetOperator.
#elif with no condition breaks the preprocessor, and MPI_Comm is used unconditionally, so the serial build fails.
The new header uses '#elif' without a condition for the serial branches and declares an MPI_Comm member unconditionally, so a build without MPI fails to compile.
The new HypreEuclid::SetOperator queries the MPI communicator from the old matrix A (which may already be destroyed) instead of new_A before resetting Euclid.
HypreEuclid::SetOperator queries the communicator from the old matrix *A, which may already be destroyed when the operator is replaced, instead of from new_A.

The new ElementRestriction::BooleanMask runs a plain host for-loop but gets its pointers with Read()/ReadWrite()/Write(), which are device pointers when a GPU backend is active, so the host dereferences device memory.
The new ElementRestriction::BooleanMask loops on the host over pointers obtained with Read()/ReadWrite()/Write(), which are device pointers when a GPU device is active.

fix_subject: Fix for parallel transfer operators on CPU
defect: TrueTransferOperator is built as P_h^T T P_l (RAPOperator) instead of R_h T P_l, so true-dof transfer sums contributions of shared/constrained dofs and gives wrong values.
TrueTransferOperator uses RAPOperator(P_h, T, P_l), i.e. P_h^T T P_l, instead of R_h T P_l, so in parallel shared true dofs are summed instead of restricted and the transferred vector is wrong.
The 3D lexicographic face DOF maps for hex faces 0, 1 and 4 have the reversed in-face orientation relative to MFEM's face vertex ordering, so the normals are wrong.

The new GetFaceDofsLex maps 3D hex faces 0 (bottom), 1 (south) and 4 (west) in plain lexicographic order, which does not match the faces' outward-oriented reference ordering, so face DoFs and normals come out flipped.

x_out_loc/x_loc are now allocated with GetVSize() and then re-pointed with SetData(x_out.GetData()), which leaks the owned buffer; in TMOPDescentNewtonSolver the min det(J) loop also reads x_loc before any values are written to it.

x_out_loc and x_loc are allocated with fes->GetVSize() and then repointed with SetData(x_out.GetData()), which leaks the allocation; the DescentNewton min-det loop also reads x_loc before it holds values.

fix_subject: Fixed Mesh::UniformRefinement for an all-tet mesh and the 1D case.
defect: The new branch ref_algo == 1 && meshgen == 1 also catches 2D triangle (and 1D) meshes, sending them to LocalRefinement instead of uniform refinement.
The new 'ref_algo == 1 && meshgen == 1' branch, meant for all-tet meshes, also catches all-triangle (and 1D) meshes and sends them to LocalRefinement instead of the uniform 2D refinement.
ParallelAssemble(Vector &tv) skips the MultTranspose when there is no prolongation matrix and leaves tv unassigned.

ParallelAssemble(Vector &tv) now skips the work when there is no prolongation matrix and leaves tv unassigned instead of copying the local vector, giving a wrong (uninitialized) result e.g. for ex9p on one process.
RightSolve applies the pivot row swaps for X <- X P in forward order, but they must be applied in reverse order, so the result is wrong whenever pivoting occurs.
RightSolve applies the pivot swaps for X <- X P in forward order, but right-multiplying by the permutation needs them in reverse order, so the solution is wrong whenever pivoting occurred.

fix_subject: Bug fixes in GetValues methods (thanks to unit testing)
defect: The simplified GetValues/GetVectorValues no longer call T.SetIntPoint before GetValue/GetVectorValue (which use T for CalcPhysShape/CalcVShape), and GetVectorValues passes a column reference that GetVectorValue may resize, so values are wrong.

The simplified GetValues/GetVectorValues call GetValue/GetVectorValue without T.SetIntPoint(&ip) (needed by CalcPhysShape/CalcVShape), and GetVectorValues hands a vdim-sized column reference to GetVectorValue, which resizes it to spaceDim.

fix_subject: Fix sign errors in normal computation
defect: GetSigns changed the set of reference faces with positive normal sign from {0,3,4} to {0,1,4}, giving wrong normal orientation for faces 1 and 3.
The change switches the faces whose normal sign is flipped in GetSigns from face_id 0,3,4 to 0,1,4, which gives wrong normal signs on hex faces 1 and 3.

fix_subject: Fixing errors in new geometry entries
defect: The new tetrahedron Orient definition lacks the 'const int Geometry::' prefix and InvOrient lacks a terminating semicolon, so geom.cpp does not compile.
The new tetrahedron Orient definition lacks its 'const int Geometry::' type prefix and the InvOrient initializer lacks its closing semicolon, so geom.cpp does not compile.
The new TetDofOrd loops run to pm2 and use pm3 and offsets for p-2 instead of the tetrahedron interior-dof size (p-3), so the interior dof permutations index wrongly.

The new TetDofOrd interior-DOF loops run over i+j+k < pm2 instead of pm3 (there are only (p-1)(p-2)(p-3)/6 interior DOFs) and use a wrong index formula, so they write out of bounds and produce wrong reordering tables.
The new templated kernels::CalcInverse computes the adjugate with TAdjDet but comments out the division by the determinant, so it returns adj(A) rather than inv(A).
The new templated kernels::CalcInverse computes only the adjugate with TAdjDet and leaves the division by det commented out, so it returns adj(A) instead of A^-1.
FaceMatrixInt::AddMult adds the product of block 0 with X side 0 into Y side 1 and block 1 with side 1 into side 0, so the face sides are swapped.

FaceMatrixInt::AddMult adds the product of block A(:,:,0,f) with side-0 values into side 1 of y and block 1 into side 0, i.e. the two face sides are swapped relative to how the face data are assembled.
The DGTrace EA face kernels write with Write() and '=' instead of accumulating, so with several face integrators each one overwrites the previous ones' face matrices.

The new DGTrace EA kernels use Write() and '=' on the face EA arrays, which the extension passes to every face integrator in turn, so each integrator overwrites the contributions of the others instead of accumulating them.
TransposeIntegrator::AssembleEAInteriorFaces swaps the int0 and int1 blocks when transposing, although each element's own-face block stays on the same side; debug Print calls were also left in.

TransposeIntegrator::AssembleEAInteriorFaces swaps the two interior blocks (int0 to int1) when transposing, although each interior block belongs to its own element and only its indices should be transposed, so the result is wrong; it also leaves debug Print calls in.

fix_subject: Fixed saving/loading of empty elements. Parallel NC I/O seems to work.
defect: Replacing leaf_elements traversal with a loop over all elements testing !ref_type also treats freed/unused element slots (parent == -2) as leaves in the destructor, PrintBoundary and the loaders.
The new loops over all elements with a !ref_type test (destructor, PrintBoundary, both loaders) also treat freed or unused element slots (parent == -2) as leaves.

fix_subject: Add tests for FiniteElementSpace Ordering::ByVDIM and bug fixes to have it work correctly
defect: For byVDIM spaces the new ProjectQuadratureDiscCoefficient reorders the element result into interleaved order before SetSubVector, but element vdofs are always listed component by component, so the values land in the wrong dofs.

The new ProjectQuadratureDiscCoefficient manually reorders each element's vector from byNODES to byVDIM for byVDIM spaces, but element vdofs are already listed component by component, so values end up in the wrong places.

In the parallel BR2 setup the offset arrays are not resized for face-neighbor elements (out-of-bounds writes), the loop uses i <= GetNE() instead of i < GetNE(), the transformation uses index i instead of inbr, and ExchangeFaceNbrData is not called.

In the new parallel BR2 constructor the offset arrays are sized for local elements only but written for face-neighbor elements, the neighbor count uses GetNFaceNeighbors (ranks) instead of face-neighbor elements, the test 'i <= GetNE()' is off by one, and the neighbor transformation is requested with i instead of inbr.
PA.C0.HostWrite() was moved before SetSize, so after the reallocation the host values are written to memory that is not marked valid on the host.
PA.C0.HostWrite() is hoisted before PA.C0.SetSize(...), which reallocates, so the following host writes to C0(0) happen without a valid host-write flag and the device copy can be stale.
The cuSPARSE path is taken whenever useCuSparse is set (on by default), even when the device is not CUDA, so host data goes to cuSPARSE or, without CUDA, the multiply is skipped.
AddMult now takes the cuSPARSE branch when useCuSparse is set (on by default) without checking that a CUDA device is active, so CPU runs go into the cuSPARSE/empty branch and skip the CPU SpMV.

fix_subject: Fixed the new PA interpolators to work on device and added the CUDA flag to the unit tests, for inclusion in cunit_tests.
defect: The new test_multiplicity reciprocal and the xscaled scaling loop index Vectors on the host with operator(), without HostReadWrite, after device MultTranspose; on GPU builds they read stale data.

The new test_multiplicity computation and the x scaling in AddMultTranspose use host-side element access on vectors that MultTranspose/the caller fill on the device, so with a GPU backend they read stale host data and give wrong results.
The TETRAHEDRON case has no break and falls through into the HEXAHEDRON case, reading verts[4..7] of a tet, and the hex face edge ordering is wrong.

The new DataCollectionToFmsDataCollection builds hex (and tet) faces from hand-written edge orders that do not follow MFEM's element edge/face ordering, lacks a break after the TETRAHEDRON case so it falls through to the hex code, and divides the triangle count by 4.

fix_subject: Fix the logic to transpose faces in ElementAssembly.
defect: The new in-place (add == false) transpose of interior-face exterior blocks loops only over j > i, so the diagonal entries of A_ext(.,.,0) and A_ext(.,.,1) are never swapped, and the face transpose is wrong.

The in-place (add == false) transpose of the interior-face exterior blocks only swaps pairs with i<j, so the diagonal entries are never exchanged between sides 0 and 1 and the off-diagonal side mapping is incomplete; the result is not the transpose.

The change computes mixed_faces = mesh->GetNumGeometries(2) > 1 unconditionally, whereas before it was evaluated only when the mesh had faces, so for meshes with dim < 2 it calls GetNumGeometries with dim > Dim and trips its assertion.
mixed_faces = (mesh->GetNumGeometries(2) > 1) is now evaluated for every mesh, which trips the dim <= Dim assertion in GetNumGeometries on 0D/1D meshes; it used to be called only when faces exist.

fix_subject: Fixed problem in new NCMesh::UpdateVertices, seems to work now.
defect: The new UpdateVertices numbers ghost vertices from 0 (NGhostVertices++), so their vert_index values collide with owned vertex indices, and the vertex_nodeId map built over NVertices+NGhostVertices gets owned entries overwritten by ghost nodes.

The rewritten UpdateVertices numbers ghost vertices from 0 (NGhostVertices++), overlapping the owned-vertex indices, and only then builds vertex_nodeId over all of them, so owned entries are overwritten.

fix_subject: Fix a bug in the size of I.
defect: The I array is allocated with size entries, but the CSR row pointer needs size+1 and h_I[ndofs] is written, a heap overflow.
GetFullAssemblySparseMatrix allocates the CSR I array with size entries instead of size+1, so h_I[ndofs] and the shift loop write past the end.

fix_subject: Fixed an error that came up during tests. Now the gradient operator always works on ldofs, including the diagonal computation.
defect: The new OperatorJacobiSmoother(ess_tdofs, damping) constructor creates a Solver of size 0, and SetOperator takes N from op.Height() although AssembleDiagonal may be on tdofs, so sizes are wrong.

The new OperatorJacobiSmoother(ess_tdofs) constructor leaves the Solver at size 0, and SetOperator sets N = op.Height(), which is wrong for operators that act on ldofs but whose AssembleDiagonal is on tdofs.

fix_subject: Fixed an error that came up during tests. Now the gradient operator always works on ldofs, including the diagonal computation.
defect: Gradient::AssembleDiagonal returns a true-dof diagonal (asserting TrueVSize and applying P^T) while the Gradient operator is ldof-sized (Operator(fes.GetVSize()), Mult on ldofs), a size and space mismatch.
Gradient::AssembleDiagonal now asserts a true-dof-sized diagonal and applies P^T, while the Gradient operator itself acts on ldofs (sized fes.GetVSize()), so the diagonal does not match the operator.
The I-array scan loops to size+1 and writes h_I[size+1], one past the end of the size+1 array allocated just above.
The I-array prefix sum loops to size+1 and writes h_I[size+1] (and the shift loop reads/writes I[size+1]) although I has only size+1 entries, an out-of-bounds access.
The rewrite contains '#ifdef MFEM_USE_CEEDit = mymap.begin();', which disables the whole body; it also erases with an undeclared iterator 'it' and calls CeedBasisDestroy on restrictions.
The rewritten RemoveCeedBasisAndRestriction has a garbled `#ifdef MFEM_USE_CEEDit = mymap.begin();`, calls erase(it) on an undeclared iterator, and destroys restrictions with CeedBasisDestroy.

fix_subject: fixing test_constrainedsolver to pass with HYPRE BigInt
defect: The new ParallelTestProblem passes int arrays (row_starts_a, row_starts_c, col_starts) and Blocal.GetJ() to HypreParMatrix constructors expecting HYPRE_Int*, which fails to compile with HYPRE big-int.
The new ParallelTestProblem passes int row_starts/col_starts arrays and SparseMatrix int J to HypreParMatrix constructors that expect HYPRE_Int, so the unit test does not compile with HYPRE big-int.

fix_subject: Fix use_nodes logic for TargetConstructor inside ComputeElementTargetsPA
defect: Moving the 'needs nodes' early return before TargetConstructor::ComputeElementTargetsPA makes discrete-adaptivity targets (and GIVEN_FULL) return without setting up Jtr when GetNodes() is null.

Moving the 'nodes not set' early return in front of targetC->ComputeElementTargetsPA makes every target type other than IDEAL_SHAPE_UNIT_SIZE (including GIVEN_FULL analytic and discrete adaptive targets) return before the target constructor's own PA path is tried.

fix_subject: Fixed an ordering issue on high order z-directed edge dofs
defect: SegDofOrd[1] negates the z-directed (non-tangential) edge dofs for reversed orientation, although those dofs should only be reordered, not sign-flipped.
The reversed-orientation dof map negates the z-directed edge dofs (SegDofOrd[1][p+i] = -1 - (2*pm1 - i)) although these out-of-plane components do not change sign when the edge orientation flips.

fix_subject: Fix reading XML VTK meshes with zlib enabled
defect: The new XML VTK path saves tellg() and seekg()s back to the start of the stream, which fails on zlib-compressed (gzstream) input that cannot seek.
Mesh::Loader rewinds the stream with tellg/seekg before reading an XML VTK mesh, which fails on non-seekable compressed (zlib ifgzstream) inputs.

fix_subject: Fix bug when using closed uniform LOR
defect: refiner.SetType(ref_type) passes a BasisType value where GeometryRefiner expects a Quadrature1D type, so closed-uniform LOR refines with the wrong point type.
The LOR mesh constructor calls refiner.SetType(ref_type) with a BasisType value although GeometryRefiner::SetType expects a Quadrature1D type, so closed-uniform LOR uses the wrong point set.

fix_subject: Fixed R_hp matrix for 3D, renamed to HpConformingRestriction, documented.
defect: The if/else was replaced by a conditional expression whose operands are GetGhostDofs (void) and GetEntityDofs (int), which is ill-formed C++ and fails to compile.
The change turns the if/else into a conditional expression whose operands are GetGhostDofs (returns void) and GetEntityDofs (returns int), which is ill-formed C++ and does not compile.

fix_subject: Fixes a bug in pumi.cpp mentioned in #2161
defect: rotateSimplex uses an assignment (type = apf::Mesh::TET) instead of a comparison in the else-if, so any non-triangle type is treated as a tet and type is overwritten.
rotateSimplex uses assignment `else if (type = apf::Mesh::TET)` instead of comparison, which overwrites type and makes the unsupported-type branch unreachable.

The change replaced vec_fe->GetDim()==2 with vec_fe->GetVDim()==2 for the cross_2d rotation, which is wrong for subclasses whose vector shape comes from a scalar FE (e.g. MixedScalarCrossGradIntegrator, VDim 1) instead of the overridable vdim = GetVDim(*vec_fe).

MixedScalarVectorIntegrator now tests vec_fe->GetVDim() == 2 for cross_2d; for gradient-based integrators vec_fe is a scalar H1 element (VDim 1), so the 2D cross rotation is skipped and the result is wrong.
The attribute index j is reused as the inner vertex-loop counter and only incremented per rank, so attr_ne[j] reads the wrong attributes; the send is also guarded by ne instead of nc.

In PrintAsOne the attribute index j is reused as the vertex loop counter and incremented once per rank rather than per element, so wrong attributes are printed (and the array can be read out of bounds); attributes are also sent under if (ne) instead of if (nc).

fix_subject: fix wrong operator pointer in ProductSolver
defect: After renaming members, the ProductSolver initializer Solver(A->NumRows()) now refers to the not-yet-constructed member OperatorPtr A instead of the parameter A_.

After the parameter was renamed from A to A_, the ProductSolver constructor's Solver(A->NumRows()) now refers to the not-yet-constructed member OperatorPtr A instead of the parameter, which is undefined behaviour.

fix_subject: Fix GetNumGeometries check in FESpace on empty meshes.
defect: Turning MFEM_ASSERT into MFEM_VERIFY on GetNumGeometries(dim) makes FiniteElementSpace construction abort in all builds on meshes with no elements (e.g. empty MPI ranks).

Turning MFEM_ASSERT(mesh->GetNumGeometries(dim)) into MFEM_VERIFY makes FiniteElementSpace construction abort in every build on a mesh with no elements (for example an empty MPI rank), where GetNumGeometries is 0.

fix_subject: Fixing Project methods on R2D classes
defect: The new RT_R2D_FiniteElement::Project(fe,...) scalar branch multiplies the 2x2 adjugate by a 3-vector normal leaving vk[2] uninitialized, and the vector branch omits the Trans.Weight() scaling of the z-component.

In the new RT_R2D_FiniteElement::Project(fe,...), the scalar branch multiplies by the 2x2 adjugate, so vk[2] is never set yet is used for d < vdim (3), and the vector branch leaves out the Trans.Weight() factor on the z normal component.
The pyramid vertex count uses nx*nx*nz instead of nx*ny*nz, and the center vertex index VTXP(x, y+1, z+1) is offset instead of VTXP(x, y, z).

The pyramid branch of Make3D adds nx*nx*nz center vertices instead of nx*ny*nz and uses the center vertex VTXP(x, y+1, z+1) instead of VTXP(x, y, z), so the vertex count and pyramid connectivity are wrong.
The new serial unit test declares 'HYPRE_Int size', but HYPRE_Int is undefined in non-MPI builds, so the unit tests fail to compile in serial configurations.
The serial test case in this new unit test declares 'HYPRE_Int size', a type that does not exist in serial (non-hypre) builds, so the unit tests fail to compile there.
The setup kernels reshape COEFF as (NQ, NE) and read C(q,e) even when the coefficient is a size-1 vector (null or constant Q), which reads out of bounds.
For a null or ConstantCoefficient the coefficient vector has size 1, but the new setup kernels always reshape it as NQ x NE and read C(q,e), an out-of-bounds read giving garbage coefficients.

fix_subject: Fix a couple of issues that came up in nightly testing.
defect: The new LinearWedgeFiniteElement constructs NodalFiniteElement with the default FunctionSpace::Pk, although the wedge space is not Pk, unlike H1_WedgeElement which uses Qk.

 *    F̂ n = ½(F(u⁺,x)n + F(u⁻,x)n) - ½λ(u⁺ - u⁻)

 * @note The implementation assumes monotonous |dF(u,x)/du⋅n| in u, so the
 * maximum characteristic speed λ for any interval [u⁻, u⁺] is given by
 * max(|dF(u⁺,x)/du⁺⋅n|, |dF(u⁻,x)/du⁻⋅n|).
 */

{
public:

    * (num_equations)
    * @param[in] state2 state value (u⁺) at a point from the second element
    * (num_equations)
    * @param[in] nor normal vector (not a unit vector) (dim)
    * @param[in] Tr face element transformation
    * @param[out] flux F̂ n = ½(F(u⁺,x)n + F(u⁻,x)n) - ½λ(u⁺ - u⁻)
    * @return max(|dF(u⁺,x)/du⁺⋅n|, |dF(u⁻,x)/du⁻⋅n|)
    */
   real_t Eval(const Vector &state1, const Vector &state2,
               const Vector &nor, FaceElementTransformations &Tr,
               Vector &flux) const override;

   /**
    * @brief  Jacobian of normal numerical flux F̂(u⁻,u⁺,x) n
    * @note The Jacobian of flux J n is required to be implemented in
    * FluxFunction::ComputeFluxJacobianDotN()
    *
    * @param[in] side gradient w.r.t the first (u⁻) or second argument (u⁺)
    * @param[in] state1 state value (u⁻) of the beginning of the interval
    * (num_equations)

    * (num_equations)

    * @param[out] grad Jacobian of F(u⁻,u⁺,x) n
